items.title: What Does AT&T Stock Do To Your Money When The Market Falls?
items.summary: AT&T (T) is up 4.4% over the last five trading days, while the S&P 500 is down 1.1%. Strength in a weak tape pulls money in. That five-day move is not the question. The question is what holding AT&T does to your money when the market moves, because over the past year it has tended to go the other way.

items.title: Is Comcast Stock Cheap Or Just Shrinking?
items.summary: Comcast (CMCSA) generated free cash over the past twelve months worth 20.1% of its market value. The median S&P 500 company manages 4.4%. Part of that gap is Comcast's debt. The rest means one of two things: the market has made a mistake, or the cash is about to get smaller. Comcast keeps losing broadband customers, and that is the market's answer.

items.title: Prime Video Scores 5-Streamer Bundle
items.summary: The package consists of Prime Video and niche streaming platforms - AMC+, BritBox, MGM+, PBS Masterpiece and Starz - for $29.99 a month, offering a savings of nearly 39% vs. subscribing to each service individually.

items.title: Is Verizon Stock Counting On Money That Has Not Arrived Yet?
items.summary: Verizon Communications (VZ) has had a good year. The stock returned about 24% over the past twelve months against roughly 19% for the S&P 500, and at about $51 it sits at the top of its one-year range. The turnaround is real. What is not real yet is the revenue meant to pay for it.

items.title: Is AT&T Asking You To Fund A Network For AI Traffic?
items.summary: AT&T (T) is running its largest year ever for fiber expansion, a plan for 8 million new locations, of which over 4 million were acquired from Lumen, and asking shareholders to keep funding it. It expects $23 billion to $24 billion of capital investment in 2026, and the roughly $18 billion of buybacks and dividends is essentially all the free cash flow left.
